To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

head-to-object alignment is an overestimation of head position by about 10% of head rotation and that the perceptual interpretation (and possibly the representation) of head position is improved by the presence of visual afield.
head position is underestimated with respect to a visible object (e.g., a scale mark) by 7% when the head is rotated by 45° to the right or left.
head position is perceived as shifted toward a visual object and that this misalignment is reduced in the dark by the addition of visual afferences.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the perception of head position in space.
the perception of head position and its role in head-eye coordination.
the question of how the brain combines information about head and eye movements to achieve an accurate representation of gaze position and to control gaze direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the perception of head position with respect is a complex function of visual and proprioceptive afferents and that the perception of visual objects in space is a function of head position and eye position.
the perceptual system of head position with respect is not a linear function of head position with the visual field, but is rather a non-linear function of head position and of the visual field.
the perception of head position in space is an imperfect representation of the actual physical head position.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the perception of angular head and eye positions is not a direct function of the proprioceptive signals, and that the visual afferents are not only important in providing the information for the perception of the angular positions of the head and eyes, but they may also play a role in improving the interpretation of the proprioceptive information.
the percept of head position with respect in a visual object is a function of the interaction between visual and proprioceptive information.
, when the eyes are shifted by head movement, the percept of angular head position relative to the visual object is shifted as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the perceptual interpretation and representation of head position is a complex process involving a variety of sensory inputs.
head and object position do not coincide in a visual scene.
head position is perceived in a manner that is consistent with the idea of a head-centered frame of reference.
